newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - US PRODUCER PRICES OFF 0.1 PCT JULY.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - US PRODUCER PRICES OFF 0.1 PCT JULY.

text.p: Following are comments from U.S. economists after the Labor Department said the Producer Price Index (PPI) fell 0.1 percent in July after declining 0.1 percent in June. Core PPI, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, fell 0.1 percent.
Economists in a Reuters survey had forecast both overall and core PPI up 0.1 percent.

THOMAS CARPENTER, CHIEF ECONOMIST AND MANAGING DIRECTOR, A.S.B. CAPITAL MANAGEMENT: "We have had seven consecutive months ... of declines in the Producer Price Index. This is unprecedented in U.S. economic history.
"What this means from the (Federal Reserve) standpoint is that it's virtually impossible to increase the level of fed funds on August 19."
CARY LEAHEY, CHIEF U.S. ECONOMIST, HIGH FREQUENCY ECONOMICS:
"You have another excellent PPI report. You can use the old quip that there are probably more sightings of Elvis this year than there have been of rising inflation in the PPI.
"It's very impressive. You don't see any inflation in the pipeline from this series if you look at intermediate goods."

JAMES PADINHA, ECONOMIST, BRIEFING.COM: "People will make a lot out of the seventh straight decline and I would say it's encouraging. Even the core intermediate index was unchanged and the core crude index was down a little, so those over the past year or so have been showing, if you look at a graph, they're still below the zero line."

"Overall the U.S. inflation picture is not overly threatening...keep in mind, however -- as we're seeing ... in Britain -- that you don't have to have a wholesale acceleration to have upward pressure on retail prices." No text received

ASTRID ADOLFSON, SENIOR VICE PRESIDENT AND SENIOR ECONOMIST, MCM MONEYWATCH INC: "We've had so many consecutive months of decline in the PPI. In the core, we've had a sharp decline in car prices. The surprise was that car prices fell as much, and of course that helped push the whole thing down."
(( -- N.A. Treasury Desk, 212-859-1660 )) No text received
